holidays.name: National Panda Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the world's fluffiest black-and-white bamboo enthusiast. Watch panda cam videos, wear panda gear, or learn how conservation work is helping these gentle giants thrive.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, popular with animal lovers and conservation fans.
holidays.funFact: Giant pandas can spend 10 to 16 hours a day eating, and a single panda may munch through 26 to 84 pounds of bamboo daily.

holidays.name: National Everything You Do Is Right Day
holidays.description: Today is your official permission slip to feel great about every choice you make. Wear the mismatched socks, eat dessert first, and take a victory lap for it.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, meant as a lighthearted boost of confidence.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists have long found that people who practice self-compassion tend to bounce back from mistakes faster than those who are hard on themselves.

holidays.name: National Freedom of Information Day
holidays.description: A nerdy but noble day celebrating the public's right to know what its government is up to. It's a good day to request a public record, visit an archive, or thank a librarian.
holidays.origin: It is observed on March 16, the birthday of James Madison, the fourth U.S. president, who championed open government and an informed public.
holidays.funFact: James Madison, born on March 16, 1751, stood just about 5 feet 4 inches tall and is often called the Father of the Constitution.
